# 周易傳註

**ID:** KR1a0140
**Custom ID:** ZB1a0139

**Source:** 四庫全書 文淵閣版, V47.1, p1
**Extent:** 7 卷
**Base edition:** WYG

## Authors / Editors
- 李塨 (清朝) 撰 1659 - 1733

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A Yōngzhèng-period *Yìjīng* commentary in seven juàn (with appended *Zhōuyì shì kǎo* 周易筮考 in one juàn) by [李塨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%A1%A8) Lǐ Gōng (1659–1733), the principal pupil of [顏元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A1%8F%E5%85%83) Yán Yuán and chief Yán-Lǐ 顏李 school transmitter. The work was composed and revised over a decade: drafted in *Kāngxī guǐwèi* 康熙癸未 = 1703 (covering through *Guān*); continued in spring of *jiǎshēn* 甲申 (1704) at [李斯義](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E6%96%AF%E7%BE%A9) Lǐ Sīyì's house in Běijīng (completing the hexagrams); revised in autumn of the same year at [溫德裕](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%BA%AB%E5%BE%B7%E8%A3%95) Wēn Déyù's office in Yǎnchéng 郾城; the *Xìcí* and other Wings completed in *bǐngxū* 丙戌 (1706); revised in *rénchén* 壬辰 (1712) winter at [鄭知芳](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E7%9F%A5%E8%8A%B3) Zhèng Zhīfāng's house in Zǎoqiáng 棗強; further revised three or four times.

The work's argumentative core: the *Yì* was made for human affairs (*Yì wèi rén shì ér zuò yě* 易爲人事而作也). Lǐ holds, against the entire late-Sòng / Yuán-Míng / chart-tradition, that the canonical reading should foreground the human-and-ethical rather than the heavenly-and-metaphysical. He follows Confucius's *Xiàng* statements as evidence: even where the trigram-symbols name natural phenomena (heaven-and-earth, *jiànshùn* 健順, cloud-and-thunder, *Tún* difficulty), the formula necessarily concludes with *jūnzǐ yǐ* 君子以 ("the gentleman thereby"), grounding the symbolic reading in human conduct. Methodologically Lǐ accepts *xiàng* (symbol) as principal but uses *hùtǐ* 互體 jointly; for Hàn-period material he draws extensively on [李鼎祚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%BC%8E%E7%A5%9A) Lǐ Dǐngzuò's *Jíjiě* ([KR1a0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0009)); for recent material he draws on [毛奇齡](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E5%A5%87%E9%BD%A1) Máo Qílíng's *Zhòngshì Yì* ([KR1a0126](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0126)) and *Tú shū yuán shùn biàn* and on [胡渭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%83%A1%E6%B8%AD) Hú Wèi's *Yìtú míng biàn* ([KR1a0138](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0138)).

The work's deliberate omissions are substantive: refutation of *guà biàn* under *Sòng* hexagram; refutation of *Hétú-Luòshū* doctrine in the *Xìcí* gloss; refutation of *xiāntiān* eight-trigram doctrine in the *Shuōguà* gloss. Elsewhere the work simply elucidates canonical meaning without rebutting old doctrines — Lǐ's *fánlì* says "of the earlier Confucians' debates I cannot list a volume's worth; only where it greatly bears on the canon do I unavoidably argue." The *Sìkù* editors regard the work as substantively important: although Lǐ's polemical preface "is unavoidably excessive," his return of the *Yì* to *rén shì* "deeply attains the sage's import in transmitting instruction." Their summary diagnosis of the late-Míng *Yìxué* problems Lǐ corrects against — *xīnxué* 心學 readers who insert Chán *gě* 禪偈 to gloss the canon, *xiàngshù* readers who proliferate diagrams and forget the canonical text — is one of the more pointed critical statements in the *Yì*-class tíyào.

**Abstract**

Composition is fixed by Lǐ's own preface to a sequence of revisions over 1703–1712; the bracket here adopts that range. The preface (translated above in the source) records four named locations and a sequence of revisions across nearly a decade.

The work is the principal Yán-Lǐ school *Yì* commentary, applying the school's *shí xué* 實學 (practical-learning) emphasis on human affairs to the canonical *Yì*. As such, it is one of the more methodologically distinctive early-eighteenth-century *Yì* commentaries: methodologically aligned with the high-Qīng *kǎozhèng* on chart-and-numerology (drawing on Máo Qílíng and Hú Wèi) but doctrinally distinct in its Yán-Lǐ practical-Confucian orientation. The combination is unusual.

The *Sìkù* editors' qualified endorsement is substantial: they grant Lǐ the diagnosis of the late-Míng problems but warn against excessive polemic. The pairing with the contemporary [魏荔彤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%AD%8F%E8%8D%94%E5%BD%A4) Wèi Lìtóng *Dà Yì tōng jiě* ([KR1a0136](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0136)) — also Yōngzhèng-period, also methodologically reformist, also held by the *Sìkù* editors as somewhat polemically excessive — is instructive: both reflect the early-eighteenth-century willingness to depart from the late-Míng / Kāngxī court orthodoxy.

The appended *Zhōuyì shì kǎo* (one juàn) extends the work to milfoil-divination practice — paralleling [王弘撰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%98%E6%92%B0) Wáng Hóngzhuàn's [KR1a0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0125) of an earlier generation but more compact.
